candidate_decisions.reason: All three traced roles have supplied ayah and word-index coordinates and return through the focus refusal: fear supplies the adverse horizon, acceptance supplies the preceding criterion, and protection supplies the self-guarding contact. The two unresolved context branches are retained as attributed evidence without invented glosses or facets.

The supplied trace lands every branch in the focus or in 5:29-5:31 and gives each a distinct role in the movement from hand-extension through killing to concealment. The unresolved context branches have exact coordinates and a focus return, so they remain attributed rather than excluded.

The focus killing terms and the supplied 5:32 life-preservation and totality coordinates form a bounded singular-life-to-human-totality delta with a direct focus return. The unresolved context branches are retained as attributed evidence and no semantic branch is omitted.

The branch-distant acceptance reading has an exact focus carrier, independent forgiveness and repair context in 5:34 and 5:39, an explicit temporal change, and a stated containment boundary. Its exploratory status qualifies the reading but does not remove it.

findings.title: Refusal as enacted self-guarding
findings.claim: The refusal enacts self-guarding at the bodily threshold where the brothers' acts have already been differentiated by divine acceptance.
findings.mechanism: The focus fear word meets the preceding occurrences of acceptance and protection in 5:27; that context turns the unextended hand from an isolated moral declaration into the practical act of refusing to reproduce the aggressor's conduct.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the refusal as a conduct that makes the preceding criterion of guardedness visible in the threatened encounter.
findings.containment: The fear remains the focus speaker's restraint, and the 5:27 acceptance criterion remains contextual evidence; this does not claim that 5:27 grammatically determines the response or that the reconstructed HFT inference removes the live alternative.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and 5:27 surface coordinates support the contact, while the reconstructed legacy-unbound HFT trace and unresolved context branch records require attributed qualification.

branch_activations.boundary: This does not make the contextual inference a grammatical translation of the fear verb or claim that 5:27 alone specifies the response.

branch_activations.boundary: The branch record is unresolved; this preserves the attributed role without supplying an independent gloss or claiming a complete lexical definition.

findings.title: The earliest arrest point
findings.claim: The refusal is the earliest arrest point in a chain that would return guilt to the actor, make killing tractable, complete it, and leave the survivor learning how to cover its aftermath.
findings.mechanism: The focus hand-extension and killing terms meet the successive 5:29-5:31 occurrences of burden returning, self-facilitation, completed killing, digging, and concealment; the contact changes one withheld counterstroke into the first controllable break in that sequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the unextended hand as stopping a process before it recruits the self and consumes later agency in guilt and aftermath.
findings.containment: The later ayat supply a sequence and the causal arrest is an attributed inference; they do not by themselves establish a general psychology of action or erase the plain refusal of one immediate counterstroke.

epistemic.reason: Every traced stage has a supplied focus or context coordinate and a focus return, but the chain is carried by a reconstructed legacy-unbound HFT record with unresolved context branches.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The refusal stops the chain at its earliest controllable hand movement.
branch_activations.boundary: The physical hand-extension remains the carrier; the arrest-point relation is a contextual inference, not a replacement gloss.

findings.title: One life opens onto a human world
findings.claim: The single life endangered in the focus can be heard as a human world when 5:32 pairs killing or preserving one life with humanity in its completeness.
findings.mechanism: The focus killing verbs supply the threatened single body, while the 5:32 occurrences of preserving life and gathering the whole supply the scale-changing counterpart; the contact returns through the focus's universal Lord-of-the-worlds title.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the refusal as protecting more than the speaker's private moral state: one withheld lethal act bears the weight of a world of relations.
findings.containment: The singular-to-total relation is an attributed contextual inference from 5:32; it does not claim that the later legal analogy retrospectively changes the literal focus scene or that preserving and killing are disambiguated into one exclusive reading.

epistemic.reason: The focus and 5:32 coordinates are exact and the return through the focus is clear, but the HFT source is reconstructed and the two context branch records are unresolved.

findings.title: Nonextension leaves repair time open
findings.claim: As a contained root-play, the refusal preserves a future in which wrongdoing can be covered and conduct repaired, adding temporal affordance to the immediate stopping of retaliation.
findings.mechanism: The focus b-s-t form is supplied with the acceptance-of-an-excuse branch, while 5:34 forgiveness and 5:39 repair provide independent future-oriented contacts; the refusal therefore leaves time open for covering wrong and restoring conduct.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive nonextension as keeping a future response possible, not only blocking the present hand movement.
findings.containment: The physical hand-extension remains the primary carrier. This is a branch-distant root-play or temporal affordance, not a direct lexical translation of the focus participle, and the forgiveness and repair sequence need not be read as evaluating this speaker specifically.

epistemic.reason: The focus carrier and 5:34/5:39 coordinates are supplied and the HFT trace states an explicit containment boundary, but the source is exploratory, reconstructed, and two context branches are unresolved.

findings.title: Private restraint and public consequence
findings.claim: The withheld hand is a personal boundary inside a wider pericope that distinguishes private retaliation from public response to violent corruption.
findings.mechanism: The focus repeats the physical hand as the instrument of a refused personal killing, while the supplied 5:33 hand occurrence appears with killing, corruption, and a distinct legal response; their connection marks the boundary between the two situations.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold restraint and accountability together: the refusal does not erase consequence, and public judgment is not the same act as private vengeance.
findings.containment: The context supplies a contrastive boundary only. It does not claim that the speaker cites 5:33, that the focus states a public legal rule, or that every threat warrants the later response.

epistemic.reason: The focus hand branch is lexically accepted and the 5:33 Arabic plus connection note supplies the contrast, but the context row does not supply target morphology or lexical analysis.

findings.title: The worlds become waymarked
findings.claim: The explicitly added Fatiha path context lets the focus's worlds also be heard as a field of waymarks, making the speaker's restraint part of a world whose direction can be read.
findings.mechanism: The focus occurrence of al-alamin carries the supplied sign-and-waymark branch, and the separate path occurrences in Fatiha 1:6 and 1:7 provide the road contact that activates its way-guiding facet.
findings.reader_payoff: The universal title gains a local sense of legibility: the world is not only where conduct occurs but also where orientation can be found.
findings.containment: The ordinary worlds reading remains intact. This is an external overlay from the individually supplied 1:6 and 1:7 occurrences; it does not announce a whole-surah path thesis or make every Fatiha word active here.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch and its waymark facet are supplied, while the external context is a lean root-and-word projection and the branch identity is qualified.

findings.title: The title becomes provision-shaped
findings.claim: The explicitly added Fatiha context lets the focus title be pictured as a provisioned world: abundant gathered water and a water-rich well meet the Lord-of-the-worlds designation when 1:7 supplies an irrigation and provision contact.
findings.mechanism: The focus occurrences of Rabb and al-alamin carry the supplied water branches, and the exact external 1:7 provision-and-irrigation occurrence provides an independent contact that turns the title's universal scope into a depicted sustaining field.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the universal title as a world being supplied and sustained, which gives the focus's restraint a concrete human setting.
findings.containment: The water image is an external overlay, not the direct translation of Rabb or al-alamin. The sea and water-rich-well alternatives in the al-alamin branch remain separate, and no whole-surah water system is asserted from this local contact.

epistemic.reason: The two focus branch records and the external 1:7 root-and-word cue are supplied, but the water branches carry qualified and reframed lexicon identities and the context is lean.

friction_notes: All four supplied HFT records are reconstructed legacy-unbound evidence; unresolved context branches are therefore retained with attributed roles, null glosses, and null facets.

The external 1:5 projection supplies the surface root ع و ن while also exposing a mapped ع ي ن cue for water imagery; because that cue does not agree with the supplied root, it was not activated. The Fatiha provision overlay relies on the exact 1:7 provision-and-irrigation occurrence instead.
External 1:2 repeats the Rabb al-alamin title but adds no independent semantic detail beyond the native title, so it does not receive a separate finding.
The 5:33 connection supplies exact Arabic and a stated private-versus-public boundary but no target morphology or lexical analysis, so the resulting contextual finding remains qualified.
